rv.q: It’s beautifully lit by Bruno Poet – the whole thing glows – and there are moments of real power and poetry in the writing, eloquently delivered in particular by Ashley McGuire and Trystan Gravelle.
I’d recommend the production to anyone who doesn’t know the play, while still feeling that it works best when presented with a minimalist austerity that matches Churchill’s text.
However, it is also a flinty play with little humour and scant theatricality; a case of ‘Give me metaphor or give me death.’
By the end, I envied Charles I the loss of his head.

cn.t: Churchill's civil war play receives mixed reviews: critics praise the text's radical power and ambition, but question whether Turner's epic production with 62 actors overwhelms rather than serves the intimate 1976 original.
